newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank shelves bank ownership plan.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank shelves bank ownership plan.

text.p: Thai central bank governor Rerngchai Makaranond said his bank was shelving for now a proposal to consider raising a 25 percent equity limit that foreigners can hold in Thai banks.

Rerngchai said late on Tuesday he did not expect any quick change in permitted foreign ownership limits in Thai banks and finance firms as his bank regards the issue only as a proposal for future consideration.
He said the issue was first floated by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan, who believed increased future foreign equity participation in Thai banks may strengthen their competitiveness.
"It is just an idea for the future when our market is further deregulated. I did not expect my remark (earlier this week) would be sensitive to bank stock prices," he said.

Brokers said reports on a central bank move to raise the foreign ownership limit in Thai banks this week had hurt bank stocks listed on the Thai bourse's foreign board where foreign owned shares are traded.
Major bank shares fetch hefty premiums on the foreign board to those on the market's main board.
